extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society, natural philosophers, physicians, surgeons, and learned readers
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting observational natural history, anatomy, geological and experimental results for a 17th‑century scientific journal (Philosophical Transactions). Emphasizes detailed description, measurements, figures, and critical evaluation of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve case histories with figures and explanatory table
rubrics_metrics.description: "thought good to preserve the history thereof, by committing it and the figure of the parts spoken of, to the press, together with a table for better explanation"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting unusual anatomical cases, publish the history together with illustrative figures and an explanatory table to make the account clear and preservable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform prolonged, careful dissection before learned audience
rubrics_metrics.description: "after (having embalmed the parts) he had made for a whole month together the particular dissection thereof at his house, before all the most curious and knowing physicians, surgeons, apothecaries, midwives, and other searchers of nature"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out extended, meticulous dissections and examine specimens in the presence of knowledgeable practitioners to validate observations and interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include labeled anatomical plates with keyed legends
rubrics_metrics.description: The page provides a Latin keyed list: "A. Pars vaginae. — B. Orificium internum matricis apertae. — C. Collum matricis. — D. Cavitas matricis..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide plates/figures labelled with letters/numbers and a corresponding key (preferably in Latin in this tradition) so readers can unambiguously identify structures described in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise chronological records of events
rubrics_metrics.description: The eruption history is recorded by years and eras: "An. 1329, until 1333, there was another. An. 1408 another. An. 1444 another... An. 1633 another..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List dates/years and sequence events precisely when reporting historical or recurring natural phenomena to allow correlation across sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report quantitative measurements and distances
rubrics_metrics.description: "digging for pumice-stones, find at the depth of 100 palmes, which is about 68 feet..." and other references to depths, thicknesses, diameters, times, distances
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measurable quantities (depths, thicknesses, diameters, distances, durations) to make observations reproducible and comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate internal versus external use when claiming medicinal effects
rubrics_metrics.description: "This author does not duly discriminate between the internal and external use of these springs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state whether therapeutic claims refer to internal ingestion or external application of mineral waters (or other remedies), because effects and evidence differ by route of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support chemical/medicinal assertions with accurate analyses or cite experienced authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whoever wishes for any thing like accurate observation... should consult the tracts written by Dr. Fyconer, and the more recent publications of Dr. Gibbes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back claims about chemical composition or medicinal powers with proper chemical observations/analyses or reference trusted chemical/medical works rather than anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note contradictions and correct erroneous assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial corrections appear: "This assertion, that the ice of these glaciers is gradually converted into stone, is founded in error."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate contributors' claims and explicitly correct misconceptions or errors, citing reasons or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reviewing books, focus on the scientific/philosophical content
rubrics_metrics.description: "we shall only take notice here of the heads it contains of a philosophical nature" (in a book-review context)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reviews for a scientific readership, summarize and critique the work's scientific or philosophical contributions rather than general narrative content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe formation processes, hazards, and economic aspects for geological observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Glacier/crystal account: "The snow... is hardened into ice... turns into a stone... Such stones closely compacted compose a whole oblong firm mountain... At the foot of these mountains crystals are with great labour dug out... sold at a good rate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report natural-formation hypotheses, associated hazards (e.g., cracking, openings covered with snow), and economic value/market information for extracted specimens to provide a full account.

rubrics_metrics.name: For experimental devices, report specifications and performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: "made another of 34 inches diameter, which melts all sorts of metals... in less than a minute of time, and vitrifies brick in the same time; ... sets [wood] on fire in a moment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing instruments or apparatus, give dimensions, observed performance (times, materials affected) and potential uses so others can assess and reproduce experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide comprehensive ethnographic/economic description of foreign lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Japan observations catalog climate, diseases, crops, metals, manufactures, printing, arts, government, religion, morals, and commerce: e.g., "The air is... salubrious... The plague has never been heard of there... Silver is there in its highest perfection... They have mathematicians..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on foreign countries, include climate, health, resources, technologies, manufacturing practices, social customs, and trade goods to inform comparative natural-philosophical and economic understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed anatomical and functional descriptions with timing and comparative notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Silk-worm monograph excerpts detail rings, muscles, vessels, 'lungs', heart, ventricle, silk glands, timing of transformations: e.g., "the aurelia... in the space of 1 min. 10 sec." and developmental timings for butterfly emergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give fine-grained anatomical descriptions (parts, fibres, vessels), functional interpretations, comparative references to other species, and measured timings for developmental events to support biological conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report observed therapeutic outcomes but flag limited or anecdotal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Bath cures are recounted (voiding stones, relief from gout) but accompanied by a cautionary footnote: "The asserted efficacy... is contradicted by the accurate observations of later writers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record observed cures and anecdotes, but explicitly note when evidence is anecdotal or contradicted by subsequent accurate observation; recommend further controlled observation.
